registry_name: Rocket Trader Public Reference Strategy Registry

references.name: Time-series momentum / trend following
references.organization: AQR Capital Management / Journal of Financial Economics
references.original_scope: 58 liquid futures and forward contracts across equity indexes, currencies, commodities and sovereign bonds; return persistence over approximately 1 to 12 months with partial reversal at longer horizons.
references.rule_hypothesis: Measure each instrument's own trailing excess return over multiple lookbacks. Positive trend may support a long position; negative trend is cash/flat in Rocket Trader's initial long-only implementation.
references.rocket_trader_adaptation: Test long-only versions on US equities/ETFs and crypto spot separately. Do not copy futures short exposure, leverage, contract roll assumptions or published results into spot markets.
limitations: The original study is not a proof that the same rule works on SPY, QQQ or crypto spot.
Its multi-month horizons are not directly comparable to intraday signals.
All adaptations require new out-of-sample tests after costs.

references.name: Cross-sectional stock momentum
references.original_scope: US stock winner/loser portfolios with holding horizons in the 3-to-12-month range.
references.rule_hypothesis: Rank a point-in-time eligible equity universe by trailing relative performance, with a skip/reversal window tested separately. Compare top-ranked securities against the broad-market benchmark.
references.rocket_trader_adaptation: Long-only top-ranked basket; no shorting. Universe membership, delisted securities, corporate actions, survivorship bias, turnover, spread and borrow-free assumptions must be handled explicitly.
limitations: The published long-short strategy cannot be copied as-is because Rocket Trader starts without short selling.
Historical results may not survive current costs, universe changes or a different holding period.
Do not rank today's constituents in historical periods unless point-in-time membership is reconstructed.

references.name: Long-history trend-following reference
references.original_scope: Historical trend-following analysis across multiple markets and long periods, extending back to the nineteenth century.
references.rule_hypothesis: Use diversified trend-following rules and risk scaling as a reference family; test robustness across market regimes rather than optimize one instrument.
references.rocket_trader_adaptation: Treat as a research design reference. Build separate long-only stock/ETF and crypto-spot variants; no futures, shorts or leverage.
limitations: Historical reconstructed performance is not a guarantee of future returns.
The source includes markets and instruments not available in the initial Rocket Trader scope.
Costs, execution and data quality must be re-estimated for each target market.

references.name: Long-horizon value, business quality and capital stewardship
references.original_scope: Long-term business ownership, intrinsic value, capital allocation and shareholder stewardship; not an intraday trading system.
references.rule_hypothesis: Use business quality, durable economics, valuation discipline and long-term capital allocation as a separate slow-horizon reference.
references.rocket_trader_adaptation: Do not use this qualitative reference as an intraday signal. It can inform a distinct long-horizon ETF/equity research sleeve only after reliable point-in-time fundamental data is available.
limitations: This is not a fully specified algorithmic rule set.
Berkshire's historical results are not an achievable benchmark for a small automated account.
Do not infer current positions from delayed public disclosures as if they were real-time orders.

references.name: Jesse Livermore — trend and loss discipline
references.organization: Historical practitioner reference, summarized in AQR research
references.original_scope: Qualitative emphasis on assessing the broad market trend, cutting losses and letting profitable trends continue.
references.rule_hypothesis: Test explicit trend filters, predefined exits and risk limits as separate hypotheses.
references.rocket_trader_adaptation: Use only to formulate testable rules. Do not treat quotations, anecdotes or claimed historical returns as statistical evidence.
limitations: No verified machine-readable trade ledger is supplied by this source.
Anecdotal success cannot populate BenchmarkEvent records.
Only independently tested quantitative rules may affect strategy selection.

references.name: Buy-and-hold benchmark
references.original_scope: Passive holding-period return of the same asset or broad-market proxy.
references.rule_hypothesis: Measure whether active strategies add net value over holding the same asset through the same dates.
references.rocket_trader_adaptation: Use as a mandatory benchmark for SPY/QQQ and as an asset-specific buy-and-hold comparator for crypto spot.
limitations: Use identical dates and include dividends/corporate actions where applicable.
A risk-matched cash or volatility-matched baseline is also required when exposures differ.
